findings.title: Three desktop bridges copy one request skeleton and check the reply echo against three different baselines
findings.anchor: 3 copies of a ~25-35 LOC skeleton; metrics run=6 overlap=0.37; co-change support=4 conf=1.00
findings.what: Each bridge re-implements stopped-guard, request, decode, echo check, metadata and stop; storage compares the echo with the validated payload, workspace with the caller object, entry with a re-decoded copy. Entry throws synchronously on invalid input, the others reject asynchronously.
findings.why: The shared core (apps/desktop/src/main/harness-request-core.ts) owns only neutral texts, so an invariant the storage comment states is already broken in a sibling. Previously recorded as #123 deep-review Q19/Q20/Q22.

steps: Pin the echo baseline and invalid-input behaviour per bridge with characterization tests.
Move the skeleton (guard, request, decode, echo against the validated payload, invalid input as envelope) into the request core; bridges supply schemas and texts only.
acceptance: All three bridges compare the echo with the validated command payload
No bridge method throws synchronously on invalid input
remediation.testStrategy: Bridge unit tests through the bridge public methods; re-pin the cross-bridge correlation rows (precedent 8a0658d).
remediation.tradeoff: Keep per-bridge copies — rejected: they already drifted.

findings.anchor: 1 of the default integrations (minidump) uploads an attachment that beforeSend never touches; gated by consent + DSN env
findings.what: Sentry.init has no integrations override, so the default minidump integration uploads raw native crash dumps (module paths, process memory) once consent is on.
